Policy Summary:
The Nigerian Minerals and Mining Act, 2007, provides a framework for the regulation, 
administration, and incentivization of mining activities in Nigeria.
The act governs the exploration, exploitation, and management of minerals in Nigeria. 
Ownership and control of minerals, water, and related resources are vested in the state.
The exploration or exploitation of minerals requires proper authority.
Certain lands are excluded from mineral exploration and exploitation.
Priority and competitive bidding processes for mineral rights.
Institutional Responsibility:
The Minister of Mines and Steel Development oversees the implementation of the Act.
Establishment of the Mining Cadastre Office and its zonal offices to manage mineral titles and maintain registers.
Creation of departments such as the Mines Inspectorate Department and Mines Environmental Compliance Department.
Establishment of State Mineral Resources and Environmental Management Committees.
Regulations and delegation of powers by the Minister
ESG / Due Diligence Elements:
Environmental impact requirements (weak)
 community obligations, safety measures
Governance & Political Economy Issues:
Elite capture of licences, 
weak enforcement and  discretionary practices
Implementation Challenges: Limited inspectorate capacity, overlapping mandates with NESREA and states
Stakeholders Impacted by the Policy:
Federal Government
State Governments
Mining Companies and Investors
Local Communities
Environmental Agencies
Miners and Artisanal Miners

Policy Summary:
Federal Government of Nigeria, which holds ownership and control of all mineral resources
 in trust for the people under the Constitution (Section 44(3)) and the Nigerian Minerals and Mining Act, 2007 (NMMA).
 The Minerals and Mining Regulations 2011 establish rules to regulate the acquisition,
 operation, and management of mineral titles in Nigeria. It outlines obligations for environmental protection,
safety standards, environmental compliance, waste disposal, community compensation, 
and corporate social responsibility in mining operations. 
Establishment of the Solid Minerals Development Fund  to drive investment and growth in the mining sector
Institutional Responsibility:
Ministry of Mines and Steel Development (MMSD)
Mining Cadastre Office (MCO)
Mines Inspectorate Department
Mines Environmental Compliance Department
Nigerian Geological Survey Agency (NGSA)
State Mineral Resources and Environmental Management Committees
ESG / Due Diligence Elements:
EIA requirements, water use conditions, 
community protection provisions
Stakeholders Impacted by the Policy:
Investors, Mining Companies, ASM, 
local communities, state agencies

Policy Summary: Sector policy focusing on mineral development, geological mapping, infrastructure, beneficiation and value-addition pathways, including incentives to local investors and attracting foreign investment through favourable trade, fiscal, and monetary measures.
ESG / Due Diligence Elements:
Weak ESG integration; focuses more 
on economic development
Governance & Political Economy Issues: Disconnect between policy intentions and licensing enforcement
Stakeholders Impacted by the Policy: Federal govt, private sector, downstream producers

Policy Name: Roadmap for the Growth and Development of the Nigerian Mining Industry
Policy Summary:
Strategic plan to reposition mining as growth engine; identifies seven priority minerals, including lithium and niobium, 
and targets midstream processing and local value chains by 2025.
ESG / Due Diligence Elements: Limited; mostly focused on investment rather than ESG
Implementation Challenges: Funding, lack of coordination among MDAs

Policy Summary:
NGSA-led programme to generate modern geophysical and geochemical data for priority minerals, including gold,
 PGM, nickel, chromium, cobolt, rare earth minerals, lead zinc, silver, copper, barite and iron ore resources in Nigeria.
Environmental standards for mining operations covering waste, emissions, water, hazardous materials and rehabilitation.
ESG / Due Diligence Elements: Pollution control, water quality, tailings safety
Governance & Political Economy Issues: Weak enforcement, agency overlap with MMSD

Policy Name: Artisanal and Small-Scale Mining (ASM) Formalisation Programme
Policy Summary: Programme to support formalisation, training, environmental management and licensing of ASM cooperatives; aims to reduce illegal mining and improve traceability.
Governance & Political Economy Issues: Weak incentives for formalisation, corruption barriers

Policy Summary: Establishes NGSA’s mandate for geological mapping, exploration data generation, archival management and national geoscience database governance.
Governance & Political Economy Issues: Legacy colonial data not digitised; poor data access

Policy Summary: Nigeria’s domestic implementation of the EITI Standard, requiring revenue reporting, licence register transparency, beneficial ownership disclosure and audits.

Policy Name: State Mining Policies & Mineral Development Companies
Policy Summary: States have created mining development companies and local regulations to participate in joint ventures, regulate community agreements and support ASM cooperatives.
Mandatory agreements between mining companies and host communities outlining benefits, compensation, employment and social investment obligations.
Governance & Political Economy Issues: Weak monitoring, elite capture within communities
